claims.text: Beregond may stem from beren meaning ("bold") and gond ("stone"). He was likely named after the steward bearing the same name.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, Part Three: "The Etymologies"

claims.text: Beregond's fathers were from the vales of the White Mountains, and prior to that they lived in Ithilien. Beregond had two sons, Bergil, who was ten years of age at the time of the War of the Ring, and a younger son named Borlas.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "Minas Tirith"; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "XVI. The New Shadow"

claims.text: Beregond was a member of the Third Company of the Citadel. He admired Faramir and saw him as a brave warrior and a great leader. Beregond did not travel outside of Minas Tirith often but understood the threat that Sauron posed to the city.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "Minas Tirith"

claims.text: Upon Aragorn's coronation on May 1st, Beregond was brought forward to receive judgement for leaving his post and for killing Denethor's guards on hallowed ground. The penalty would have been death, but the King showed mercy as the deeds were done out of love for Faramir, and Beregond was merely dismissed from the Guard of the Citadel. For his bravery in battle, Aragorn appointed him the Captain of the Guard of Faramir, which was also called the White Company. He later went to live in Emyn Arnen in Ithilien to serve his lord, Faramir, the new Prince of Ithilien.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "The Steward and the King"

claims.text: On the morning of March 9th, , Beregond was assigned to help Peregrin Took who had just become a Guard of the Citadel. As Beregond had never met a hobbit before, he was eager to meet Pippin and he was astounded that Pippin looked much like a child yet had faced more dangers than most Men of Gondor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "Minas Tirith"
claims.section: section == History == > War of the Ring

claims.text: After helping to carry Faramir to the Houses of Healing, Gandalf gave the key to the Closed Door to the injured Faramir. Beregond stood guard over Faramir at the Houses of Healing and was present when he awoke.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "The Houses of Healing"
claims.section: section == History == > War of the Ring > Battle of Pelennor Fields
